hero.title: The whole workflow in Evix —
hero.desc: Evix replaces the scriptwriter, host, editor, social media manager and analyst — and carries one brand context through every step. Below is the full loop: from the quiz to a finished video in the feed.
hero.shotAlt: Scenario list in the Evix workspace: type, avatar, voice and publishing status

cycle.title: Nine steps, one cycle
cycle.desc: Each step builds on the last: the quiz sets the brand voice, parsing decides what to film, the library holds both. Then come the script, voiceover, cover, editing and publishing.

register.title: Sign-up and login
register.desc: An account takes half a minute: first name, last name, email and password — no SMS, no long forms. One account is one brand workspace, home to scenarios, avatars, edits and connected social accounts.
list: Sign up with email and password, no SMS
Inside: scenarios, avatars, editing and social accounts
The session lives in your browser — log in and go

quiz.title: Brand quiz — the foundation of every module
quiz.desc: Twelve short questions: name, niche, audience profile and pain points, tone of voice, formal or informal address, how you monetize, key topics, restrictions, expertise, platforms and the main call to action. The answers build a Tone of Voice document.
list: 12 questions about the brand and audience
The output is a Tone of Voice document
ToV is woven into every piece of copy automatically
You can rewrite the answers at any time

competitors.title: Competitor parsing — a map of demand
competitors.desc: Add competitor accounts by hand or hit “Find automatically” — the system collects their videos from 19+ platforms: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Shorts, VK, Telegram, Zen, RuTube. Every video shows views, likes, comments, engagement, date and a direct link.
list: The data folds into a “niche core”: hooks, formats, sound design
Anti-patterns too — what doesn't work in the niche
competitors.alt: Competitor list with metrics and statuses

library.title: Data library — your brand's brain
library.desc: Everything the system knows about the brand lives in six cores. Three are built automatically — Tone of Voice, marketing and product analysis. Three accumulate as you work — the account, niche and competitor cores. Scenarios pull context from here, not thin air.
list: 3 cores from practice: account, niche, competitors
Cores can be cleaned and edited by hand
The visual-format library and favorites live here too
library.alt: Brand data cores in the library

scenario.title: Creating a scenario: pick a type
scenario.desc: A scenario comes together in five steps: type → text → avatar and voice → result → editing. It all starts with the generation logic — where the system gets the idea. There are four types:
scenario.alt: Step 1 — choosing a scenario type from four options

competitor.title: Competitor
competitor.desc: Breaks down the hooks of competitors' best videos from the niche core and writes a script along their logic.

repackage.title: Repackaging
repackage.desc: Takes your existing video and rewrites it around a new angle.

custom.title: Own topic
custom.desc: Generates from your prompt — informed by the Tone of Voice and the analytics gathered.

formats.title: Visual formats (PRO)
formats.desc: Auto-assembled from the viral-format library. Available on the Pro plan.

result.title: Text, avatar, voiceover — and a finished video
result.desc: The system writes the monologue and immediately strips stage directions, emoji and stray symbols: what's left is the hook, the body and a closing call to action. Regenerate as many times as you like. Then pick an avatar (7 hosts or your own), a voice to match its character, emotion, format and speed — the output is a 2–4 minute MP4 of your avatar speaking.
list: Text self-cleans of stage directions, emoji and symbols
7 host avatars plus your own; voice matched to character
A finished MP4 with no watermarks or filler music
result.alt: Scenario parameters and the generated video

covers.title: Covers — a hook, not a video frame
covers.desc: The system reads the script text and proposes covers around four emotions: shock, pain, fear and mystery. Each angle gets 3–4 concepts with a score, so there's something to A/B test. In two sizes at once: 9:16 and 16:9.
list: 4 emotional angles: shock, pain, fear, mystery

montage.title: Editing — automatic or manual
montage.desc: A scenario with a finished video moves to editing — trims, cuts, subtitles, cover. The status is always visible: no edit, in progress, with the editor, done. From here, two paths:

auto.title: Evix auto-edit
auto.desc: Transitions, subtitles and a cover added automatically. Ready in 5–10 minutes.

pro.title: Evix editing PRO
pro.desc: A real editor: custom effects and b-roll tailored to the specific video.

publish.title: Publishing, profile and plans
publish.desc: The finished video publishes to your connected social accounts — the same brand context reaches up to 19 platforms. In the profile you edit brand details and photo, connect social accounts for parsing and publishing, and switch between Free and Pro.
list: Publishing to connected social accounts — up to 19 platforms
Social accounts connect for both parsing and posting
Free: auto-edit, basic formats, scenario limits
Pro: editing PRO, queue priority, visual formats, expanded covers
publish.alt: Profile, social accounts and plan settings

0.text: In the first month we moved from three SaaS tools to one. Our scriptwriter started handling several times more clients, and approvals shrank from three days to one.
0.name: Anna Kuznetsova

1.text: The big thing — scripts stopped sounding "AI-generated." You load up the client's ToV and get copy that actually sounds like the product. That changes everything.
1.name: Dmitry Solovyov

2.text: I run my blog as an expert, and shooting every day just isn't possible. The Evix avatar is the only solution where my "AI self" doesn't turn into a caricature.
2.name: Maria Lebedeva

3.text: We replaced three tools with one. Scriptwriter, editor, and SMM all work in the same window — we no longer lose approvals in chat threads.
3.name: Igor Terentyev

4.text: The ToV quiz is the best way to digitize a client's brand. Each new scriptwriter used to rewrite the copy from scratch — now everyone works from one core.
4.name: Olga Morozova

5.text: A viral video used to spiral into an endless list of edits. With Evix the script comes together in an hour and lands straight in our ToV.
5.name: Alexander Nikitin

6.text: I run 4 clients on my own. Evix replaced my scriptwriter and junior editor. If I had found it on day one, I'd have saved half a year of my life.
6.name: Ekaterina Voronova

7.text: I used to edit 3 videos a day — now I comfortably ship 8. Auto-editing handles the grunt work, and I polish the parts that matter.
7.name: Nikita Zhukov

8.text: I don't enjoy filming myself. The Evix avatar sounds like me, speaks like me — and my followers can't tell the difference. It saved my blog during maternity leave.
8.name: Daria Sokolova

0.text: In the first month we moved from three tools to one. The team now ships 4× more videos, and approvals dropped from three days to one.

1.text: The main thing — scripts stopped sounding “AI-generated”. You load your own Tone of Voice and get text that genuinely sounds like me. That changes everything.

2.text: I run a blog as a doctor, and filming every day is impossible. Evix’s avatar is the only solution where the “AI-me” never turns into a caricature. Followers still don’t notice the swap.

7.text: We’re a clinic outside the capital, without a big SMM team. Evix covers all the short-form content — from script to publishing. We basically work like a studio, and patients don’t even notice.

hero.desc: What's in the product, how Free and Pro plans work, what AI does, and which social networks we support. If you don't find it — ask via the form.

0.a: Evix is an AI content studio in a single workspace: ToV quiz, client cores library, AI scripts with analysis, avatars and voices, covers, editing (auto and manual), competitor parsing, and publication tracking.

1.a: No. You post the finished video to the social network yourself, then add the publication to the tracker — with a preview, platform, date, and description. Views and likes are filled in manually or pulled in afterward.

2.q: Can scripts be created from scratch or only 'based on a competitor'?
2.a: Both options work. In the 5-step wizard, the first step is choosing the type: 'based on a competitor' (with virality analysis) or your own topic and key points. Then comes the script, avatar, video generation, and editing.

3.a: Five 'cores' are the shared source of truth for AI: client ToV, marketing and product analysis, account core (what worked), and niche core. The competitor core is currently in development.

4.q: Where do view and like metrics come from?
4.a: In the 'Publications' section, metrics update once the post goes live. The 'Statistics' section — aggregated analytics on reach and retention — is currently marked 'Soon'.

0.q: How many plans are there and how do they differ?
0.a: Two plans: Free — all modules and template-based auto-editing. Pro — the same plus manual editing by a live editor and priority on auto-editing.

1.a: Pricing is discussed individually and depends on video volume and team composition. Leave a request — we'll send a quote tailored to your case.

2.q: Is there a separate plan for agencies?
2.a: Corporate terms for network agencies with high client volume are discussed separately. Reach out via the form — we'll put together a plan tailored to your workflow.

0.q: How does Evix analyze a script?
0.a: The script is checked against groups: hook + retention (main weight), mid-tier criteria (visuals, CTA), and minor criteria. It's also cross-referenced with the ToV, marketing, and product cores, and in 'based on a competitor' mode — with the competitor itself. The output: a score, checklists, and recommendations.

1.q: Can I upload my own voice for an avatar?
1.a: You can add an avatar (photo) and a voice (audio sample) to the catalog — with a choice of gender, style, tone, and emotion. If you don't upload anything, the product uses an imitation for the preview.

2.a: You can add competitors manually, in bulk, or run auto-search by niche (platforms, region, ER, audience size). After parsing, a grid of viral videos opens up with breakdowns by hook, retention, and triggers.

0.a: In the publications tracker: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, VKontakte, and others. In competitor parsing and auto-search, additionally: VK Clips, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, Telegram, Dzen.

1.q: Where do I connect social networks?
1.a: In the client profile and in the data library, the 'Connected social networks' section. In the publication form, you can only select connected platforms.

0.q: What roles are available in the product?
0.a: Owner, technical department, script / editing / publication managers, contributors (scriptwriter, editor, publisher), and guest client access. Staff have a separate internal login with demo access.

1.q: How do I assign a client to a staff member?
1.a: When creating a client, the owner immediately selects managers (for scripts, editing, and publications). They in turn assign their own contributors. A staff member sees their own clients and locked cards of the others — for team transparency.

2.q: Can I reject a script with a comment?
2.a: Yes. Scripts and edits can be returned with a reason for rejection — the author will see the comment. The same works in the editing queue.
